note: This task's designed licence STOP condition FIRED and did NOT clear — the second of F5's two, and the one the spec warned would be harder. portrait.jpg is a White House press photograph (EXIF Artist = Pete Souza) whose embedded notice forbids reproduction or dissemination without written permission from the White House Photo Office; committing a fixture is exactly that. The image was downloaded, its metadata read, and the file DELETED, with tests/fixtures/face/ never created (commit b926819). Two escalations followed. First the human was offered a researched CC0 substitute (the Met's c.1850 '-Elderly Man; Full Face-' daguerreotype, licence verified per-file via the Wikimedia Commons API, detection confirmed at 1 face / 478 landmarks) and approved it; then the human proposed keeping the White House photo on the grounds that this is a personal project. That premise was WRONG and correcting it was the pivot of the whole episode: the notice's 'personal use only' permission is granted to the SUBJECT(S) IN THE PHOTOGRAPH, not to whoever is using it for a personal purpose. With that corrected, a third arrangement was offered and chosen — fetched-not-committed: keep portrait.jpg on the developer's machine, .gitignore it, and commit the Apache-2.0 portrait_expected_face_landmarks.pbtxt beside it. The reason to prefer it over the CC0 substitute is concrete: MediaPipe publishes expected landmarks for portrait.jpg and for no other image, so it is the only fixture against which the real-model test can assert Google's own published coordinates. The arrangement's own risk was closed deliberately rather than discovered later — a test that silently skips when the fixture is absent is the F4.5 defect class in a new shape (a green Gate proving nothing), so the test skips with an explicit reason AND spec.md 5 pins a separate presence check so the Gate cannot pass while it skips. Both amendments (fixture change, and the earlier enforcement check) went through box-2 re-approval; the agent never checked that box. Learn scan outcome: a lesson cleared the bar but OVERLAPS HEAVILY with the [Approval] guardrail added by Task 2's scan, so per learn step 4 it is proposed as an UPDATE to that existing rule rather than a fourth guardrail — namely that an asset's own embedded metadata (EXIF/XMP) should be the FIRST thing checked, since it is the most authoritative statement available and the cheapest to read, and it is what actually settled this case after eight external sources had been consulted for the model bundle. Parked in handoff.md as Pending guardrail; project.md was NOT written unapproved. No ADR: fails condition 1 — fetched-not-committed is a .gitignore line and a fetch command, trivially reversible in either direction; it is genuinely surprising (condition 2) with a real trade-off (condition 3), but that surprise is documented where a confused reader actually lands, in the fixture README. No idea was declined by the human that lacks a home: the rejected CC0 substitute and the rejected commit-it-anyway option are both recorded with their reasons in memory/decisions.md, which is that log's purpose.
